title: Attn Stack E2E Diff Notebook — Flash/KV/Batching Upgrade
content:
Purpose
-------
This note captures the end-to-end evaluation diffs observed after deploying the attention-stack upgrade (flash-attn patch v2.1, paged-KV allocator changes, and enabling continuous batching by default) in the onboarding cluster for model-micro-1 and model-micro-2. The goal is to summarize measurable regressions/improvements across quality, latency, and cost signals and propose immediate triage steps + mitigations for rollout decisions.

Executive summary (top-level)
---------------------------
- Latency: median (p50) token latency improved ~8–12% for short-context workloads. p95 increased 6–18% on long-context tests (>= 8k tokens) for model-micro-2.
- Throughput: sustained token throughput increased 17% on batched throughput tests for both models with continuous batching enabled.
- Quality: automated eval diffs show small but notable regression signals in long-context QA and multi-turn dialogue coherence for model-micro-2: drop in EM by 3.2 pts and increase in hallucination rate ~4.5% absolute on our trivia+context set.
- Cost: estimated per-token infra cost reduced ~10% for baseline traffic shapes (many short requests). For long-context heavy usage, mem thrash caused ~6% extra retries increasing effective cost in worst-case flows.

Context and experimental setup
------------------------------
- Baseline: runtime v1.9 with legacy attention kernel (nv-attn-1) + paged-KV default allocator (page-size=64KB) + continuous batching disabled.
- Candidate: runtime v2.0-rc (flash-attn v2.1 integrated), paged-KV allocator updated (adaptive page-size + soft-evict), continuous batching enabled (default max-latency=20ms).
- Models evaluated: model-micro-1 (1.4B decoder-only), model-micro-2 (7B decoder-only) — both quantized to 4-bit profile Q4_2.
- Test harness: eval-playbook v3: runs parallel buckets (short/summaries, multi-turn-dialogue, code-snippets, long-context-story, trivia-with-context). Each job runs 1k queries per promptset with deterministic seeds for sampling.
- Hardware: dedicated 80G A100 pools (same reservation for baseline and candidate).

Prompt sets and notable prompts used
----------------------------------
- short-summ: 600 prompts, avg tokens=45 (commit: promptset/short-summ-v2)
- multi-turn-dialogue: 250 conversations, avg history tokens=420, turns=7
- code-snippets: 200 unit tests, targeted for exact match on function output
- long-story: 100 prompts with 6k–12k context, objective: continue/generate final 512 tokens
- trivia-plus-context: 150 QA items where answer is in long context + distractors

Key numeric diffs (candidate vs baseline) — aggregated highlights
--------------------------------------------------------------
- model-micro-1 (short-summ): p50 latency -10% (baseline 18ms -> 16.2ms), p95 latency -6% (48ms -> 45ms), tokens/sec +19%, Rouge-L +0.4 absolute. No quality regressions flagged.
- model-micro-2 (multi-turn-dialogue): coherence F1 -1.1 absolute, hallucination rate +2.6% absolute, p95 latency +9% (96ms -> 105ms).
- model-micro-2 (long-story): EM-like metric (answer continuity) -3.2 absolute, p95 latency +18%, observed 1.4% of requests that triggered mid-generation KV-eviction fallback (retry path).
- throughput stress (batched synthetic): tokens/sec +17% at 90% util, tail latency increased 12% when page-spill occured.

Observed failure modes and hypotheses
-----------------------------------
1) Long-context KV degradation
   - Symptom: decreased QA exact-match and increased hallucinations on long-context tests for model-micro-2.
   - Hypothesis: adaptive page-size combined with soft-evict causes earlier eviction under certain access patterns, losing prefix cache fidelity -> model sees truncated or stale KV, yielding hallucinations.
   - Evidence: KV hit-rate dropped 6.8% on failing traces; eviction logs show burst evictions at seq positions ~4k and again ~8k.

2) Attention kernel numerical micro-diffs
   - Symptom: small but measurable generation differences in corner-case formatting and tokenization-sensitive outputs (code snippets).
   - Hypothesis: floating-point ordering differences in flash-attn path lead to rounding diffs that cascade in autoregressive sampling. More visible in 7B model due to larger variance.
   - Evidence: deterministic reruns with same RNG show divergence earliest at token step 24 for failing items; diff traces point to attention weight matrix entries differing ~1e-5 on average.

3) Continuous batching tradeoff on tail latency
   - Symptom: improved median but worse p95 for long-running sequences when batching spikes.
   - Hypothesis: continuous batching default (max-latency=20ms) merges near-simultaneous requests into larger batches; for long-context the KV memory pressure + batch exec schedule increases GC-like stalls in allocator.
   - Evidence: correlation between batch-size spikes (>12 requests) and allocator GC events in paged-KV logs around same timestamps.

Triage actions performed during run
----------------------------------
- Replayed 120 failing long-context traces with candidate disabled for adaptive-page-size -> EM recovered to baseline on 86/120 traces.
- Re-ran failing traces with flash-attn fallback (nv-attn-compat) -> reduced divergence but not full recovery (45/120 recovered).
- Instrumented allocator to emit per-request KV-lifetime histograms; uploaded samples to S3: s3://redwood-inference/triage/attn-upgrade/2026-03-17

Immediate mitigation recommendations (short horizon)
-------------------------------------------------
- Blocked rollout for model-micro-2 until paging heuristics adjusted. The risk window for rolling to 100% is too high given customer visible regressions on long-context features.
- Hotfix options:
  1) Disable adaptive page-size for >4B models (config toggle: paged_kv.adaptive=false) — low risk, quick revert.
  2) Reduce continuous-batching default max-latency from 20ms -> 10ms for long-context deployments (config: batching.max_latency_ms=10) — reduces batch spikes.
  3) Enable flash-attn only on short-context routes via routing policy (route tag: short-context -> flash-attn=true).
- Run targeted canary: 5% traffic on model-micro-2 with hotfix 1 + aggregated KV metrics enabled for 48 hours, compare EM and hallucination rates.

Longer-term engineering workstreams (owners suggested)
-----------------------------------------------------
- Allocator team (owner: Tomás Rivera): refine eviction policy to be access-pattern aware (priority: 2-week spike patch, 1-quarter refactor).
- Serving/runtime team (owner: Evan Brooks): implement deterministic attention numeric-compat mode to reduce micro-diffs for sensitive promptsets; provide per-model kernel selection policies.
- Applied ML (owner: Priya Shah): expand long-context promptset coverage in onboarding harness, add targeted adversarial prompts that surface KV-eviction cases earlier in CI.

Open questions / notes to self
----------------------------
- How correlated are the hallucination regressions with quantization artifacts vs KV eviction? Need ablation runs: quantized vs fp16 + candidate runtime.
- Some failing items are reproducible only under load; schedule synthetic concurrency stress with mixed-size requests to reproduce at scale.
- Consider shipping a lightweight counterfactual that logs full KV keys for failed traces (privacy review required).

Checklist for next 72 hours
--------------------------
- [ ] Patch and deploy paged_kv.adaptive=false to canary (owner: Tomás) — target: today EOD.
- [ ] Run 5% canary for 48 hours with extended telemetry (owner: SRE) — start: 2026-03-19.
- [ ] Create follow-up eval job: quantization-ablation (Priya) — include fp16 runs.
- [ ] Draft customer-facing note for any customers using long-context endpoints (GTM) — draft by 2026-03-20.

Appendix: relevant logs and short reproductions
------------------------------------------------
- Sample failing trace id: attn-upgrade-20260317-TR-00042 (repro steps included in linked_artifacts github PR).
- Quick reproduction script: ./eval/run_single_trace.sh --model model-micro-2 --trace-id TR-00042 --runtime v2.0-rc --fallback nv-attn-compat
- Quick perf checklist for reviewers: check KV-hit-rate, eviction timestamps, batch-size histograms, flash-attn numeric-compat flag.

Concluding note
---------------
The upgrade shows clear wins for standard short-request traffic (lower cost, higher throughput). However, long-context and multi-turn dialog workloads for larger models surface two orthogonal risk vectors (KV eviction heuristics and attention numeric diffs). I recommend pausing full rollout for 7B-class models and shipping targeted hotfixes + a 5% canary to validate mitigations before a wider deployment.

(End of notebook. Draft comments welcome — please add inline with suggested labels: triage/confirm/reject.)
